claims.text: A PVD-deposited nanostructured ceramic-HEA composite layer will significantly increase the surface hardness of a CoCrFeNiMo0.85-coated stainless steel substrate relative to the baseline HEA coating.
The composite layer will significantly improve corrosion resistance relative to the baseline CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating.
The as-processed CoCrFeNiMo0.85 HEA coating has a conventional microstructure and conventional surface properties.
Controlling PVD temperature can prevent thermal stress in the coating system.
PVD deposition of the composite layer will form a dense and adherent interface with the underlying HEA coating.
The ceramic phase will interlock with the underlying HEA matrix.
The dense composite layer will act as a physical barrier to corrosive attack.
The composite layer will transfer and distribute mechanical loads.
Low porosity and high barrier properties will increase corrosion protection.
Increased surface hardness and improved load distribution will limit crack initiation and propagation.
The treated surface will have a lower corrosion rate than the baseline CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating.
Improved hardness and corrosion resistance will prolong component service life under combined aggressive chemical and mechanical conditions.
The untreated CoCrFeNiMo0.85 coating has lower hardness and greater susceptibility to corrosion and wear than the proposed composite-coated surface.
The improvements will remain effective under moderate thermal conditions and exposure to 3.5 wt.% NaCl.
Extreme temperature fluctuations or chemical concentrations beyond the tested range may exceed the coating's performance limits.
Failure to achieve at least a 15% hardness increase and a 20% reduction in corrosion current density, or failure of coating adhesion, would falsify the hypothesis.
